More than $10 million investment adds nearly 100,000 square feet of covered and enclosed storage to support expanded product offerings and enhanced customer service

BOISE, Idaho--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Boise Cascade Company (“Boise Cascade” or the “Company”) (NYSE: BCC) recently celebrated the grand reopening of its Phoenix, Arizona, Building Materials Distribution (BMD) facility following an expansion and renovation representing an investment of more than $10 million. The investment significantly increases covered and enclosed storage capacity, modernizes site infrastructure, and positions the branch to expand its product offerings and better serve customers throughout the region.

The project, which began in May 2025, adds 52,500 square feet of enclosed warehouse space and two covered storage structures totaling approximately 45,600 square feet. These improvements protect building materials from Phoenix’s extreme weather while creating capacity for a broader selection of products, including timbers, decking, panels, and other specialty building materials. The expanded facility also supports the continued growth of Boise Cascade’s nationwide partnership with James Hardie®. Upgraded storage and racking systems are designed to enhance material handling, order fulfillment, and operational efficiency, while improvements to drainage, water retention, utilities, and other site infrastructure support the branch’s long-term operational needs.

“This expansion reflects our long-term commitment to the Phoenix market and to helping our customers succeed,” said Jo Barney, Executive Vice President of Building Materials Distribution at Boise Cascade. “By adding significant covered and enclosed storage, we’re able to offer a broader selection of building materials while improving the service, efficiency, and reliability our customers expect. This milestone is a testament to the dedication of our Phoenix associates and the strong partnerships that have supported our growth in Arizona.”

This branch has served the Phoenix market since the early 1970s. Today, the branch employs 64 associates and serves customers throughout Arizona and surrounding markets.

The grand reopening on November 12, 2026, brought together over 280 customers, Boise Cascade leaders, and associates to tour the expanded facility and celebrate the milestone.

About Boise Cascade

Boise Cascade is one of the largest U.S. wholesale distributors of building materials and a leading manufacturer of engineered wood products and plywood in North America. Our integrated model and national distribution footprint position us to deliver outstanding service to our customers across a broad range of industry-leading products, including key structural products that we produce. Headquartered in Boise, Idaho, we operate more than 60 distribution and manufacturing facilities strategically located across the U.S. and Canada. Our work is powered by a dedicated team of over 7,500 people. Learn more at www.bc.com.

  • New three-year strategy includes support for youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and pairs grant funding with employee volunteerism to deepen impact
  • Grant funding across three strategic commitments will support nonprofits serving communities in AZ, CT, FL, GA, IL, MO, NJ, PA, TN and TX
  • Applications open now through December 18 for nonprofits supporting patients and caregivers navigating complex health conditions

BLOOMFIELD, Conn., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Cigna Group (NYSE: CI) is deepening its community impact strategy with a focus on supporting youth mental health, veteran well-being and people living with complex health conditions and their caregivers. The strategy includes a three-year, $31.5 million commitment from The Cigna Group Foundation, the philanthropic arm of The Cigna Group, to support nonprofit organizations aligned to these areas. Informed by research identifying pressing community needs, the funding supports populations and areas where data suggests focused efforts can have a meaningful impact.

Experience the full interactive Multichannel News Release here: https://www.multivu.com/cigna/9433451-en-cigna-group-deepens-community-impact-strategy

Since The Cigna Group unveiled a refreshed approach to community engagement in 2024, the Foundation has invested more than $30 million in nearly 190 nonprofit organizations, with grant-funded projects reaching at least 321,000 people. The evolved strategy builds on that work, pairing grant funding with employee volunteerism, expertise and partnerships to help nonprofit organizations strengthen their impact in the communities they serve.

"Over the past several years, we've seen the tangible impact we can make when we invest in strong nonprofit partners and come together to help communities achieve better health and vitality," said Melissa Skottegaard, board chair of The Cigna Group Foundation. "We're building on what's working, bringing together funding, collaboration and the skills of our employee volunteers to address some of the most pressing health challenges facing communities across the street and around the world."

Three Strategic Commitments Support Health and Well-Being

Beginning in 2027, the Foundation will invest $31.5 million over three years across three strategic commitments addressing critical community needs.

  • Improving Youth Mental Health. Building on its longstanding commitment to youth mental health, the Foundation will invest $10.5 million over three years to continue supporting organizations that expand access to mental health support and resources, with a focus on meeting the growing needs of adolescents ages 12-18.
  • Enhancing Support for Veterans. The Foundation will deepen its support for veterans with a $10.5 million, three-year investment in programs that help veterans achieve greater stability through housing, employment and financial well-being initiatives.
  • Supporting Complex Care Patients. A new $10.5 million, three-year Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program will strengthen services for patients and caregivers, with initial grantmaking focused on autoimmune and inflammatory conditions, blood disorders, cancer, neurological conditions and rare diseases. Funding will help address non-clinical barriers to treatment, including care navigation, education, peer support, mental health resources and assistance with essential social needs.

"For people living with complex health conditions, managing their health requires ongoing clinical management, specialized treatment and coordination across multiple providers, treatments and support systems," said Dr. Amy Flaster, chief medical officer, The Cigna Group and board member, The Cigna Group Foundation. "I see firsthand how their needs can extend beyond medical treatment, whether it's understanding care options, finding emotional and peer support, or addressing practical needs that can make it harder to manage their health day to day."

"Community organizations can be a powerful source of support for people navigating complex health conditions," said Matt Perlberg, president of Evernorth Pharmacy & Care Delivery, executive vice president of Customer Innovation, and board member of The Cigna Group Foundation. "By helping patients and caregivers connect with resources and overcome barriers to care, these organizations can provide important support alongside essential medical treatment, helping people navigate their health and care journey."

Eligible nonprofit organizations can apply for the Supporting Complex Care Patients grant program through December 18 at 5:00 p.m. ET.

Funding Opportunities Across 10 States

Through its three strategic commitments, The Cigna Group Foundation will provide funding opportunities for nonprofit organizations serving communities in Arizona, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Texas.

Eligible nonprofit organizations may apply for two-year grants of $250,000 within the Foundation's three strategic commitment areas and defined grant program time periods, expanding community-based programs and services that help connect people with support services, overcome barriers and improve long-term health and well-being.

The Foundation will also continue supporting current grantees, including nonprofits supported through its Health Equity Impact Fund in Hartford, Connecticut, Memphis, Tennessee and St. Louis, Missouri.

Continuing National Partnership To Improve Youth Mental Health

The Cigna Group Foundation will continue its national partnership with Boys & Girls Clubs of America, building on a shared commitment to improving youth mental health and well-being, now with a greater focus on supporting adolescents.

Since 2024, the partnership has helped expand trauma-informed training efforts to more than 90% of Clubs nationwide, reaching more than 11,000 staff members, while supporting new mental health resources now available at nearly 3,500 Club sites across the country. More than 1,600 young people have been reached through The Cigna Group employee volunteer activities, and employees have contributed more than 2,000 volunteer hours in support of local Clubs.

The partnership will continue to expand access to mental health resources, strengthen volunteer engagement with local Clubs and support the well-being of young people nationwide.

Employee Volunteerism Extends Community Impact

The Cigna Group's community impact strategy pairs financial investments from the Foundation with opportunities for employees to contribute their time and expertise through hands-on and skills-based volunteerism. Together, these efforts help nonprofit partners strengthen their organizations and extend the impact of the Foundation's investments beyond grant funding.

About The Cigna Group

The Cigna Group (NYSE:CI) is a global health company committed to creating a better future built on the vitality of every individual and every community. We relentlessly challenge ourselves to partner and innovate solutions for better health. The Cigna Group includes products and services marketed under Cigna Healthcare, Evernorth Health Services or its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group maintains sales capabilities in more than 30 countries and jurisdictions and has more than 180 million customer relationships around the world. Learn more at thecignagroup.com.

About The Cigna Group Foundation

The Cigna Group Foundation is a private foundation funded by contributions from The Cigna Group (NYSE: CI) and its subsidiaries. The Cigna Group Foundation aims to support, collaborate and convene with nonprofit organizations addressing society's greatest health challenges. In addition to increasing access to programs and care in geographies demonstrating significant need, the Foundation responds with humanitarian aid relief during critical times and strengthens colleagues' support of causes through matching donations and volunteer rewards. To learn more, visit www.thecignagroup.com/community.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Seabridge Gold Inc. (TSX: SEA) (NYSE: SA) ("Seabridge" or the "Company") reported today that the British Columbia Supreme Court (the "Court") has released a decision (the "November Ruling") settling the Court Orders in respect of the Petitions brought challenging the Substantially Started Designation ("SSD") for its KSM Project in Northwest BC. Although in the November Ruling the Court ruled that when it directed the SSD back to BC's Environmental Assessment Office ("EAO") for "reconsideration" it quashed the SSD, the status of the KSM Project's environmental assessment certificate is not affected by the November Ruling and the Tahltan and Nisga'a Nations continue to strongly support the KSM Project. If, after its reconsideration of the SSD, the EAO again concludes the KSM Project was substantially started, the KSM environmental assessment certificate will continue in place and not be subject to expiry.

Seabridge Chair and CEO Rudi Fronk stated that "the legal status of KSM has not changed as of the November Ruling. We are very confident that KSM has more than met the requirements for a Substantially Started designation. We also have the full support of the principal First Nations who have recognized traditional territory and Treaty rights, respectively, in the area of KSM and with whom we have impact benefit agreements."

KSM received the SSD on July 24, 2024 in respect of the work completed at the KSM Project to that date. In its reconsideration of whether the KSM Project has been substantially started, the EAO will also consider the additional work completed at the KSM Project between July 24, 2024 and July 29, 2026. This additional data was submitted to the EAO in September and increased the construction investment at KSM from $444 million to more than $700 million.

The SSD was challenged by the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha ("TSKLH") and SkeenaWild Conservation Trust ("SCT"). The Court's ruling on June 8, 2026 required the EAO to commence a reconsideration of the SSD following an additional 90-day consultation period with the TSKLH. The 90-day consultation period concluded on September 28, 2026. The Court, in the November Ruling, also declared that the SCT Petition was dismissed without a ruling on the reasonableness of the SSD.

In the November Ruling the Court also ruled on the extent of the consultation with TSKLH required in the reconsideration process. The Company will seek information from the EAO as to whether this November Ruling will impact the time the EAO expects to take to reach a new substantially started determination but is encouraging the EAO to conclude it promptly.

About Seabridge Gold

Seabridge Gold holds a 100% interest in several North American gold projects. Its principal assets are the KSM and Bronson Corridor projects in British Columbia's Golden Triangle. Additional projects include Snowstorm in Nevada's Getchell Gold Belt, and the 3 Aces project in the Yukon. Fuel Her Power provides practical nutrition guidance, drawing on more than 20 years of Herbalife's experience working alongside female athletes

LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Herbalife today announced the launch of “Fuel Her Power,” a nutrition guide for active women designed to help better understand their unique nutrition needs and how to support energy, performance, recovery and overall wellness. The guide is part of Herbalife's Fuel Her initiative, which builds on more than 20 years of experience working alongside female athletes to make sports nutrition knowledge more accessible to women and girls at every level of sport and activity.

Fuel Her Power Nutrition Guide by Herbalife

Women's participation in sports continues to grow, yet nearly half of all female athletes aren't getting enough energy to fuel their performance1. With only 6% of athletic performance studies focused exclusively on women2, significant gaps remain in understanding women's unique fueling, recovery and performance needs. As a result, many women are left navigating nutrition decisions without guidance that reflects their physiology, life stages and athletic goals, with consequences that can impact energy, recovery, and long-term wellness.

“Fuel Her Power” translates sports nutrition science into practical guidance covering fueling, hydration, recovery, hormone health and women's evolving nutritional needs. It is designed to make insights gained through elite sport relevant to active females everywhere, whether they compete professionally, participate in recreational sports, train for personal goals or simply want to stay active and feel their best. The guide was officially introduced Nov. 12 during a Fuel Her event hosted by Herbalife and Break Sports in Los Angeles. The event brought together female athletes, nutrition experts and community members to celebrate the guide's release and advance the conversation around women's sports nutrition.

As part of the “Fuel Her Power” guide launch event, Herbalife also recognized four accomplished female athletes whose careers reflect the dedication, resilience and adaptability required to compete at the highest levels of sport. The athletes recognized included:

  • Heather Jackson: An ultra-trail runner, gravel cyclist and former elite triathlete, Jackson has six IRONMAN victories, 16 Half IRONMAN wins and four top-five finishes at the IRONMAN World Championship. She most recently won the Javelina Jundred 100-mile race and has been a Herbalife-sponsored athlete for nearly 15 years.
  • Flavia Castro: An accomplished triathlete, Castro made history as the first woman from Bolivia to win gold at the World Triathlon Development Regional Cup and the first to reach the overall podium at an IRONMAN 70.3 event. She studies biochemistry and pharmacy and has been a Herbalife-sponsored athlete for three years.
  • Arianna Fontana: The most decorated Italian Olympian in history and the most successful short track speed skater of all time, Fontana has won 14 Olympic medals, including three golds, across six consecutive Winter Olympic Games. She has been a Herbalife-sponsored athlete for nearly a decade.
  • Emma Harvey: An Olympian and one of Bermuda's top female swimmers, Harvey represented her country at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games in the 100-meter backstroke. A national record-holder across multiple swimming disciplines, she has also represented Bermuda at the Commonwealth Games and World Championships.

Herbalife supports more than 120 professional athletes, teams and sports organizations across more than 35 sports, including partnerships with elite female athletes across multiple disciplines.

To learn more about Fuel Her and access educational resources, visit FuelHer.com.

Lecanemab showed favorable results on clinical assessment scores at 18 months, including among individuals with early Alzheimer's disease (AD) who were α-synuclein positive, a subgroup associated with higher amyloid burden and faster clinical decline

TOKYO and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Eisai Co., Ltd. and Biogen Inc. (Nasdaq: BIIB) announced today that findings from an analysis of lecanemab-irmb (generic name; U.S. brand name: LEQEMBI®) treatment and α-synuclein (α-Syn) co-pathology* in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) substudy of Clarity AD in early Alzheimer's disease (AD) were presented at the 19th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease (CTAD) conference, held in Boston and online.

In AD, α-Syn co-pathology may be present alongside amyloid beta (Aβ) and tau pathologies. α-Syn co-pathology may contribute to clinical heterogeneity and disease progression in AD, but its clinical relevance in patients with early AD receiving amyloid-targeting therapy remains unclear. In Clarity AD, lecanemab demonstrated statistically significant slowing of clinical decline in participants with early AD. This post hoc analysis evaluated the prevalence of α-Syn co-pathology and the clinical characteristics associated with α-Syn co-pathology and examined changes over time in clinical assessment scores in the lecanemab and placebo groups in the overall α-Syn-tested group and the α-Syn-positive (α-Syn+) group. These findings were presented in an oral presentation "Lecanemab Treatment and α-Synuclein Co-Pathology in the Clarity AD CSF Substudy" (OC50).

Overview of the Clarity AD CSF Substudy Analysis
A total of 623 CSF samples collected from Clarity AD participants at screening or baseline were assessed using the Amprion SYNTap seed amplification assay (SAA)**. α-Syn status was determined based on the detection of α-Syn seeds in CSF and used as an indicator of α-Syn co-pathology in the brain. Among the Aβ-positive (Aβ+) participants who were randomized to lecanemab or placebo and had α-Syn test results available, 400 were included in the α-Syn-tested group.

Key Findings

  • The prevalence of α-Syn pathology was higher among Aβ+ participants than among Aβ− participants.
    Analysis of the 623 CSF samples showed that the prevalence of α-Syn pathology was higher in the Aβ+ group than in the Aβ-negative (Aβ−) group (20.4% vs. 10.0%, respectively; p=0.001 by Pearson's chi-square test).
  • α-Syn+ participants had higher baseline amyloid burden and α-Syn co-pathology was associated with faster progression in early AD
    Among randomized participants with an evaluable baseline amyloid PET assessment, mean amyloid burden was 86 Centiloids (CL)*** in the α-Syn+ group and 67 CL in the α-Syn-negative (α-Syn−) group. The difference between groups was statistically significant (p=0.016 by ANCOVA). α-Syn+ was also associated with faster clinical decline over 18 months.
  • Lecanemab slowed clinical decline in both the overall α-Syn-tested group and the α-Syn+ group
    In this analysis, lecanemab showed a slowing of clinical decline at Month 18 compared with placebo in the overall α-Syn-tested group (n=400), similar to that observed in the overall Clarity AD population. In an exploratory post hoc analysis limited to the α-Syn+ group (n=82), lecanemab also showed a slowing of clinical decline at Month 18 compared with placebo. Specifically, the reduction in decline versus placebo, as measured by CDR-SB, was 27% in the overall Clarity AD population, 26% in the overall α-Syn-tested group, and 41% in the α-Syn+ group. As measured by ADAS-Cog14, the reduction was 26%, 45%, and 43%, respectively; as measured by ADCS MCI-ADL, it was 37%, 30%, and 43%, respectively.**** These findings suggest that lecanemab provides clinical benefit in individuals with α-Syn co-pathology.

Eisai serves as the lead for lecanemab's development and regulatory submissions globally, with both companies co-commercializing and co-promoting the product and Eisai having final decision-making authority

*

α-Synuclein (α-Syn) is a protein abundant in nerve cells that plays a role in signaling at synapses. Abnormally structured α-Syn can aggregate and form deposits called Lewy bodies. Lewy bodies are a pathological hallmark of Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. In AD, α-Syn-related pathology may coexist with amyloid- and tau-related pathology in the same individual. This is referred to as α-Syn co-pathology.

**

The Amprion SYNTap seed amplification assay (SAA) detects abnormally structured α-Syn aggregates in a sample by using them as seeds and amplifying their reaction in vitro.

***

The Centiloid (CL) scale standardizes brain amyloid burden measured by amyloid PET; higher values indicate greater amyloid burden. The scale is anchored at 0 CL (the mean in young adults without amyloid plaques) and 100 CL (the mean in people with moderate AD). The mean baseline value in Clarity AD was approximately 78 CL. Plaque negativity was defined as conversion to amyloid PET-negative status (<30 CL).

****

CDR-SB assesses overall clinical status, including cognitive and daily functioning; lower scores indicate better status. ADAS-Cog14 assesses cognitive function; lower scores indicate better status. ADCS MCI-ADL assesses daily functioning and independence in people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

BOSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Eastern Bank has been named by the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) as the top lender to small businesses for SBA 7(a) loans in Massachusetts for the 18th consecutive year.

“Eighteen years in a row demonstrates the enduring commitment of small business owners advancing businesses every day in neighborhoods from the Merrimack Valley and North Shore, to Greater Boston, the Cape, South Shore and beyond, and our team of bankers and colleagues who are deeply committed to understanding their needs and helping to turn them into thriving businesses,” said Quincy Miller, Vice Chair, President and Chief Operating Officer of Eastern Bank. “We are grateful to work alongside the SBA and many community organizations to support small businesses across Massachusetts, and proud to offer our support in New Hampshire and Rhode Island where Eastern also ranks among the top 10 SBA lenders. Helping local entrepreneurs access the resources to help their businesses succeed is core to our mission as a leading community bank.”

The SBA issues its rankings annually, based on the number of loans originated by banks in the SBA fiscal year, which runs from October 1 to September 30. In fiscal year 2026, Eastern originated 296 SBA 7(a) loans in Massachusetts totaling approximately $33.6 million. SBA loans are intended to help businesses that may not qualify for conventional loans get the funds they need to start, grow and expand. Borrowers can use 7(a) loans to meet needs that include acquiring, refinancing or improving real estate and buildings; funding working capital; refinancing existing business debt; purchasing machinery, equipment and supplies; and financing ownership changes.

Valérie Coullet’s growth from a home-based business to multi-site business owner has been supported with assistance from Eastern Bank and two SBA 7(a) loans. Coullet founded Le Petit Four, the Little Oven in her home kitchen, building a loyal following for her authentic French pastries and freshly baked breads. In 2024, Eastern provided SBA financing to open the bakery’s first retail shop in Wellesley, MA, and this year a second SBA loan funded a warehouse bakery in Needham, MA, expanding production and supporting a growing team. “Eastern Bank has been with me every step of the way, from my home kitchen to our first shop in Wellesley and now our production facility in Needham,” said Coullet. “The team takes the time to understand my business vision and as demand has grown, made the financing process seamless so I could stay focused on what I love, baking for my customers. I would strongly recommend Eastern Bank to small business owners during any phase of their business journey, whether starting out, addressing growing demand and navigating steady growth.”

Meeting will address Phase 2 study design and potential regulatory pathways for oral NEO212

CALABASAS, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NeOnc Technologies Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTHI) (“NeOnc” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for central nervous system (CNS) cancers, today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has rescheduled the Company’s End-of-Phase 1 Type B meeting concerning oral NEO212 from the previously announced date of November 17, 2026, to Monday, November 23, 2026.

At the meeting, NeOnc intends to seek FDA feedback on its NEO212 clinical development program, including the proposed patient population, trial design, endpoints and dose selection for the Phase 2 portions of the NEO212-01 trial, as well as potential regulatory pathways for NEO212. The meeting provides an opportunity for discussion; its scheduling does not establish FDA agreement on a trial design or eventual approval of NEO212.

The meeting follows completion of the Phase 1 dose-escalation portion of the NEO212-01 Phase 1/2 clinical trial. NeOnc previously reported that dose escalation was discontinued following a dose-limiting toxicity at 810 mg, administered once daily on Days 1 through 5 of a 28-day cycle, and that 610 mg was selected as the recommended Phase 2 dose. In September 2025, FDA authorized the Company to proceed with the Phase 2a and Phase 2b portions of NEO212-01.

NeOnc has also reported encouraging clinical activity observed during the Phase 1 portion of the trial. In one patient with recurrent IDH1 wild-type, MGMT-methylated glioblastoma (GBM), treatment with NEO212 resulted in a partial response, including an approximately 60% reduction in tumor size, followed by prolonged disease control lasting 21 treatment months. In a second patient with lung cancer metastatic to the brain who had previously received and progressed following multiple lines of therapy, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, treatment with NEO212 was associated with stable disease lasting approximately 16 months. While these individual patient outcomes do not establish efficacy and require confirmation in larger studies, they provide the clinical rationale for further evaluation of NEO212 in the Phase 2 portions of the NEO212-01 trial.

“We believe the durable activity NEO212 showed in Phase 1, together with a well-defined recommended Phase 2 dose, gives us a compelling foundation for the next stage of development,” said Amir F. Heshmatpour, Executive Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of NeOnc. “We look forward to discussing our Phase 2 plans with the FDA as we work to advance NEO212 for patients with CNS cancers who urgently need new options.”

Management anticipates hosting an investor webinar following issuance and receipt of the FDA’s official meeting minutes to discuss the Agency’s feedback and the Company’s anticipated next steps for the NEO212 development program. The Company expects to announce the webinar date, time and registration details separately.

About NEO212

NEO212 is an investigational oral conjugate of temozolomide and NEO100. It is being studied for CNS cancers, including recurrent glioblastoma. Preclinical studies support further evaluation of its potential activity and delivery characteristics; clinical efficacy and safety have not been established. NEO212 is being developed under an FDA investigational new drug application.

NeOnc Technologies Holdings, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing therapies for central nervous system cancers. Its investigational programs include intranasal NEO100 and oral NEO212. NEO212 has completed Phase 1 dose escalation and is advancing toward Phase 2 development. As economic and technological change accelerates, TD will deploy its philanthropy and capabilities to improve access to jobs, housing, and entrepreneurship

MOUNT LAUREL, NJ, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TD Bank Group ("TD") today announced a $2 billion (US$1.4 billion) commitment to Building Financial Strength in communities across North America over the next ten years.

Key takeaways:

  • TD will target $2 billion in philanthropy over the next ten years to help people Build Financial Strength
  • TD is initially focusing its philanthropy in three areas: workforce development, housing, and small business support

As part of this sharpened focus, TD will deepen its partnerships with community and national organizations and concentrate the Bank's philanthropy, people, and expertise where they can help Build Financial Strength at a meaningful scale.

  1. Jobs and skills development: to help workers and business owners build the skills, including essential AI capabilities, to succeed as work changes
  2. Housing affordability: to expand access to more affordable places to live and create more pathways to homeownership
  3. Small business and entrepreneurship: to enable more people to start and grow businesses, particularly where access to opportunity remains limited

"The global economy is changing at an extraordinary pace. Millions of people across North America are seeing new opportunities, yet also facing new challenges. As TD invests in our business and in the success of our clients, we have an equally important responsibility to invest in the financial strength of our communities," said Raymond Chun, Group President and CEO, TD Bank Group. "As we live our promise, to be More Human, we're acting with greater focus, concentrating our resources where we can make the biggest difference, and expanding opportunity in the communities we serve."

Economic pressures are already affecting families across North America. Recent data shows that 30% of Canadian households are experiencing difficulties meeting their financial needs, and 27% of Americans are unable to fully pay their bills each month. Building Financial Strength means creating the conditions for people and communities to move forward and overcome these challenges; because a job can change a life, a home can anchor a family, and a small business can transform a community.

To learn more about TD's impact, visit: https://www.td.com/us/en/about-us/community

FAQ

  1. What does TD do to support communities?

    TD's community giving is focused on helping people Build Financial Strength by supporting organizations that are helping people access good jobs, affordable housing, and small business support. TD is targeting $2 billion (US$1.4 billion) in community giving over ten years to support this work.

  2. What are TD's philanthropic priorities?

    TD's community giving is focused on workforce development, housing, and support for small businesses. Research shows these areas are critical to economic mobility, and increasing access can help people Build Financial Strength.

  3. How much does TD donate to communities?

    TD is targeting $2 billion in community giving over the next decade. This builds on the $1 billion TD provided to community organizations between 2018 and 2025.

  4. What are some examples of TD's community investments?

    As part of its community giving, TD announced donations for three organizations in Canada helping to expand access to jobs, housing, and small business supports: CILAR, Habitat for Humanity, and Jumpstart Refugee Talent.

About TD Bank Group

The Toronto-Dominion Bank and its subsidiaries are collectively known as TD Bank Group ("TD" or the "Bank"). TD is the sixth largest bank in North America by assets and serves 28.2 million clients in four key businesses operating in a number of locations in financial centres around the globe: Canadian Personal and Commercial Banking, including TD Canada Trust and TD Auto Finance Canada; U.S. Banking, including TD Auto Finance U.S. and TD Wealth (U.S.); Wealth Management and Insurance, including TD Wealth (Canada), TD Direct Investing and TD Insurance; and Wholesale Banking, including TD Securities and TD Cowen. TD also ranks among North America's leading digital banks, with more than 14 million active mobile users in Canada and the U.S. TD had $2.1 trillion in assets on July 31, 2026. The Toronto-Dominion Bank trades under the symbol "TD" on the Toronto Stock Exchange and New York Stock Exchange.

How TD Supports Communities

Supporting communities has long been part of how TD shows up for the people and places we serve. Through our philanthropy, we support nonprofit organizations that help people access jobs, housing, and create pathways to start or grow a business. Together, this work advances our commitment to Building Financial Strength by helping to create more opportunities for people and communities to thrive.

Dieppe, New Brunswick--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Colibri Resource Corporation (TSXV: CBI) ("Colibri" or the "Company") is pleased to announce the appointment of Ashley Nadon, MBA, CPA, as Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective November 19, 2026. Ms. Nadon succeeds Camilla Cormier, who is stepping down from her role as CFO to devote more time to her family. Ms. Cormier will continue to serve as a member of Colibri's Board of Directors.

Ms. Nadon is a Chartered Professional Accountant with extensive experience providing financial management, accounting and regulatory compliance services to publicly traded companies. She currently serves as CFO for several TSX Venture Exchange-listed junior resource exploration companies, with responsibilities including the preparation of financial statements, Management's Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), regulatory filings and corporate compliance.

Ms. Nadon holds a Master of Business Administration in Accounting from McMaster University's DeGroote School of Business and has been a member of CPA Ontario since 2018.

Ian McGavney, President and CEO of Colibri, commented:

"We are very pleased to welcome Ashley to the Colibri team. Her experience working with TSXV-listed resource companies and her familiarity with the financial reporting and regulatory requirements of junior exploration companies make her an excellent fit for Colibri.

"On behalf of the Board, I would also like to sincerely thank Camilla for her dedication, professionalism and contributions during her tenure as CFO. We appreciate her assistance in ensuring a smooth transition of responsibilities."

Ms. Cormier will assist with the transition of CFO responsibilities to ensure continuity in the Company's financial reporting and regulatory obligations.

Redesigned fireplace brings instant ambiance to indoor and covered outdoor spaces with real flame, refined design and no installation required.

GRAPEVINE, Texas, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Building on a growing portfolio of innovative products that continue to evolve the way people gather around fire, Solo Stove, the leading outdoor lifestyle brand within Solo Brands (OTCQB: SBDS), announces the launch of Lloyd™ 2.0. The freestanding fireplace brings the warmth and glow of real flame into the home or onto your patio, transforming everyday spaces without the need for a chimney, permanent installation or complicated setup.

An evolution of the original Lloyd, Lloyd™ 2.0 brings a refined mid-century-modern silhouette, real, cozy warmth, and thoughtful details designed for the spaces where life happens. From movie nights and quiet evenings with a book to long conversations with friends, Lloyd™ 2.0 brings an effortless glow to moments big and small. Designed for indoor spaces and covered patios, it features a flat back that fits neatly against walls, a wide, sturdy base for stability, and a built-in aroma tray to personalize the atmosphere. Fueled by Solo Stove Pure Gel Fuel, its clean-burning flame crackles and dances like a wood fire, without the mess of a wood-burning fireplace. Lloyd™ 2.0 is available in two consumer-preferred colors, Sunkissed orange and Graphite grey.

"There's something about having a real fire in the room that instantly changes how a space feels," said John Larson, CEO of Solo Brands.

"We wanted to make it easier to bring that feeling home. Lloyd™ 2.0 combines beautiful design with easy setup, putting fireside evenings within reach," said Markus Allemann, SVP Product Development.

Key Features of Lloyd™ 2.0:

  • Smokeless Fireplace
    Fueled by Solo Stove Pure Gel Fuel, Lloyd™ 2.0 delivers a clean-burning flame designed specifically for enclosed environments with no smoke, soot, or residue. Available in two colors: Sunkissed and Graphite.
  • Fits In—and Stands Out
    Mid-century modern inspired look with a space-saving flat-back design that also helps radiate heat for cozy nights.
  • Built-In Aroma Tray
    An integrated aroma tray lets the warmth of the flame gently disperse your favorite scents from essential oils or wax melts throughout the room.
  • Easy to Start & Extinguish
    Light and extinguish in seconds — no hassle, no wait.
  • Safety-Focused Features
    Designed with a low center of gravity and a protective glass barrier.
  • Real Heat, Directed Outward
    Designed to provide cozy warmth and inviting ambiance throughout your space with 9,000 BTUs directed outward when all three cans are lit.
  • Durable Steel Construction
    Built with premium materials and backed by Solo Stove's limited lifetime warranty.
  • No Installation Required
    Use indoors or in covered outdoor spaces like patios or gazebos. No mounting, fuel lines, or setup required. All you need is Solo Stove Pure Gel Fuel and a lighter.

This holiday season, Lloyd™ 2.0 is featured in Solo Stove's "Gifts That Don't Suck" campaign starring NFL legend Marshawn Lynch. Bringing his signature personality and humor to holiday gifting, Lynch encourages shoppers to skip the forgettable presents and give gifts worth gathering around. Lloyd™ 2.0 joins Solo Stove's lineup of products made to bring people together and make the holidays more memorable.

"Lloyd™ 2.0 is a perfect gift for someone who wants to make their home feel a little cozier," said Liz Vanzura, CMO at Solo Stove. "It's designed to make everyday life feel a little more special, whether you're winding down after a long day or having friends over. It's not just about having a fireplace, it's about making those moments at home feel more memorable."

Lloyd™ 2.0 retails for $549.99 and is available at SoloStove.com. Follow Solo Stove on Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok for the latest product news and updates.

Solo Brands, headquartered in Grapevine, TX, is a leading omnichannel lifestyle brand company. Leveraging e-commerce, strategic retail partnerships, and physical retail stores, Solo Brands offers innovative, premium products across four outdoor lifestyle brands: Solo Stove, known for the world's most popular smokeless fire pits including the all-new Summit 19.5™, Summit 24™ and Summit 27™ smokeless fire pits, and Infinity Flame™ Propane Fire Pits, award-winning pizza ovens, the new innovative Windchill™ Cooler, the new premium Steelfire™ Griddle, and outdoor accessories; Chubbies, a premium casual apparel and activewear brand; ISLE, maker of inflatable and hard paddle boards; and Oru Kayak, innovator of origami folding kayaks.

AM Best also has affirmed the Long-Term ICR of “bbb-” (Good) of the parent holding company, Stewart Information Services Corporation (headquartered in Houston, TX) [NYSE: STC]. The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

The ratings reflect Stewart’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management.

Stewart’s underwriting and operating metrics are expected to remain in line with industry averages despite the underlying economy and changes in interest rates, which could affect Stewart’s production and premium volume. Amid industry headwinds, Stewart’s ratings consider the group’s very strong levels of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), as well as its positive underwriting and investment results over the most recent five-year period. Stewart's earnings stability and business diversification is supported by its position as the fourth-largest title insurance writer in the United States, as well as its extensive geographic diversification across all 50 states, including its broad international presence. Stewart’s strategic acquisitions of companies that complement real estate closing solutions helps to mitigate its concentration as a monoline title insurance writer.

Negative rating action could occur if challenges from high interest rates and a slowing economy pose a significant decline in Stewart’s operating profitability and/or a material decline in its risk-adjusted capitalization levels.

  • Innovation Partnership Awards recognize Magna’s collaboration with BMW on the EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps and with Jetour on the DHD Duo Hybrid Drive 
  • Automotive News names Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam a PACE Pilot Innovation to Watch 
  • New honors bring Magna’s all-time Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot recognitions to 16 

AURORA, Ontario, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Magna has received two 2026 Automotive News PACE Innovation Partnership Awards, recognizing its collaboration with BMW on the EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps and with Jetour on the DHD Duo Hybrid Drive system. Both technologies are in production. Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam, a pre-commercial bio-based seating material, was also named a 2026 PACE Pilot Innovation to Watch.  

The three awards show the breadth of Magna’s innovation capabilities across vehicle systems, from battery enclosure design and electrified powertrains to more sustainable seating materials. Each addresses a key industry challenge with technology built for real-world production and scale.

“This is a tremendous recognition of our teams and their ability to turn complex challenges into innovative solutions,” said Eric Wilds, Chief Strategy & Commercial Officer at Magna. “Whether it’s creating smarter ways to maximize space within a battery enclosure, delivering a flexible hybrid architecture or reducing the carbon footprint of essential materials, these innovations demonstrate what’s possible when Magna’s engineering and manufacturing expertise comes together with close customer collaboration.”

Magna’s EV Battery Enclosure with OptiForm™ Endcaps incorporates the company’s proprietary OptiForm™ stamping process to create near-rectangular, high-precision corners with tight radii. The approach increases available battery space by up to 10% while streamlining manufacturing. 

Magna’s DHD Duo is a scalable hybrid drive system designed to help automakers balance performance, efficiency and cost across multiple vehicle configurations. Now in series production, the system demonstrates Magna’s speed-to-market capabilities, moving complex, high-voltage propulsion technology from development to production at scale in less than 18 months. 

Magna’s EcoSphere™ Bio-Based Foam integrates renewable resources into both the resin blend and the isocyanate components of polyurethane foam. The approach enables up to 20% renewable content while maintaining high-performance foam properties and reduces CO₂ generation by 18% compared to traditional polyurethane foam.  

The Automotive News PACE Awards recognize commercialized innovations from automotive suppliers for superior innovation, technological advancement and business performance, while PACE Pilot recognizes pre-commercial innovations with the potential to transform the automotive industry. With this year's three awards, Magna has now received 16 Automotive News PACE and PACE Pilot recognitions over its history.
